kept.q: A fixed mass of gas occupies 400 cm^3 at a pressure of 100 kPa. If the temperature is kept constant and the pressure is increased to 200 kPa, what is the new volume of the gas?
kept.explanation: By Boyle's law, P1V1 = P2V2 at constant temperature. So 100 x 400 = 200 x V2, giving V2 = 200 cm^3. The volume reduces because pressure has doubled.

kept.q: A balloon contains gas with a volume of 300 cm^3 at a temperature of 27°C. If the pressure is kept constant and the temperature is raised to 127°C, what is the new volume of the gas?
kept.explanation: Convert to Kelvin: T1 = 27+273 = 300K, T2 = 127+273 = 400K. By Charles' law, V1/T1 = V2/T2, so V2 = 300 x 400/300 = 400 cm^3.

kept.q: A sealed gas cylinder has a pressure of 2 atm at a temperature of 300K. If the volume is kept constant and the temperature rises to 450K, what will the new pressure be?
kept.explanation: By the pressure law (Gay-Lussac's law), P1/T1 = P2/T2 at constant volume. So P2 = 2 x 450/300 = 3 atm. Pressure rises because the gas molecules move faster and hit the walls harder.

kept.q: A fixed mass of gas has a volume of 600 cm^3 at a pressure of 150 kPa and a temperature of 300K. If the pressure changes to 100 kPa and the temperature changes to 350K, what is the new volume of the gas?
kept.explanation: Using the combined gas law, P1V1/T1 = P2V2/T2. So V2 = (P1 x V1 x T2)/(T1 x P2) = (150 x 600 x 350)/(300 x 100) = 1050 cm^3.

kept.q: According to the kinetic theory of gases, why does the pressure of a fixed mass of gas in a closed, rigid container increase when the gas is heated?
options: The molecules move slower and collide with the walls less often
The molecules move faster, hit the walls more often and with greater force
The molecules increase in size as they absorb heat
The number of gas molecules in the container increases
kept.explanation: Heating a gas increases the average kinetic energy of its molecules, making them move faster. Faster molecules collide with the container walls more frequently and with greater force, which increases the pressure.

kept.q: A fixed mass of gas has a volume of 250 cm^3 at a temperature of 17°C. If the pressure is kept constant, at what temperature (in °C) will the volume become 500 cm^3?
kept.explanation: First convert 17°C to Kelvin: T1 = 17+273 = 290K. By Charles' law, V1/T1 = V2/T2, so T2 = 500 x 290/250 = 580K. Converting back to Celsius: 580 - 273 = 307°C.
